title: $160B in one quarter: the profit nobody actually earned
description:
$160B in one quarter: the profit nobody actually earned

Four companies reported more than $160 billion of "other income" for Q2 2026. Alphabet filed $97.9 billion for the quarter ending June 30. Amazon filed $53.4 billion, about three times the quarter before. Nvidia and Microsoft made up the rest.

None of that came from selling a chip, an ad, or an hour of cloud. It is the fair value accounting rule: when an equity stake you already hold rises in value, the increase is recognised in the income statement as profit, before a single share changes hands. SpaceX's June listing at a $1.77 trillion valuation repriced every holder at once.

The gains are real on paper. The open question is what the same rule prints when the marks go the other way.
